shots.say: Ten Angus cows. Two days. Three cameras. One thousand seven hundred forty-nine clips.
We built a vision pipeline that watches the pen around the clock, detects what each cow is doing, and looks for the early signs of respiratory disease.
On day two, feeding fell sharply at midday — at one PM, from twenty-seven percent to under one percent — while lying time rose.
Less eating, more lying. That's a pattern a veterinarian would investigate first.
We could not identify individual cows across clips, so we report the herd signal honestly instead of inventing a ranking.
All of it ran on a single laptop, no cloud.
The full evidence is in the technical brief and the repository.
